claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is a single-phase, typically FCC material.
A minor Ti addition to CoCrFeNi will induce a dual FCC/BCC microstructure.
The induced BCC phase will occur as coherent particles within the FCC matrix with strong coherent interfaces.
Ti-alloyed CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than pristine CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
Ti-alloyed CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than pristine CoCrFeNi from room temperature through 800 °C.
The dual-phase structure will enhance dislocation pinning.
The dual-phase structure will minimize thermally activated softening at elevated temperatures.
The Ti-induced dual-phase structure will maintain higher hardness at elevated temperatures.
Ti-rich regions will oxidize during high-temperature sliding to form a thin, stable TiO2-based layer.
The TiO2-based surface layer will act as a solid lubricant at high temperatures.
Retention of hardness and formation of a lubricating oxide layer will reduce friction.
Retention of hardness and formation of a lubricating oxide layer will reduce wear rate.
Pristine CoCrFeNi exhibits increasing friction coefficients at elevated temperatures.
Pristine CoCrFeNi exhibits higher wear rates at elevated temperatures.
Thermally induced softening causes the elevated-temperature tribological deterioration of pristine CoCrFeNi.
Increased dislocation mobility causes the elevated-temperature tribological deterioration of pristine CoCrFeNi.
The proposed performance benefit is valid in ambient air from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C under standard tribological loads.
